# Phase 13 — Large GCG Suffix Dataset Analysis (§17)

**Generated by:** `scripts/phase13_suffix_analysis.py` (CPU-only, deterministic, rerunnable). Reads only on-disk raw artifacts under the four GCG bases; reuses `scripts/gcg_advbench_llm_taxonomy.py::categorize`, `scripts/gcg_7a_behavior_analysis.py::{load_manifest,load_results,per_behavior_success}`, and `scripts/build_gcg_source_of_truth.py::analyze_free_gen`.

**Deliverables:** `results/SUFFIX_TAXONOMY.csv`, `results/CATEGORY_TRANSFER_MATRIX.csv`, this file.

### §17.1 columns: EXIST (read from artifacts) vs DERIVED

| §17.1 concept | status | source |
|---|---|---|
| suffix_str / suffix_ids | EXIST | `FINAL_CANDIDATES.jsonl` (line 0) |
| suffix_length | EXIST | `CONFIG.json:gcg.suffix_length` |
| optimization seed | EXIST | `CONFIG.json:gcg.seed` |
| model identity | EXIST | `CONFIG.json:model_name_or_path`, `model_family` |
| selection_mode | EXIST | `FINAL_CANDIDATES.jsonl:selection_mode` / `objective.selection_mode` |
| evaluation score | EXIST | `FREE_GENERATION_RESULTS*.jsonl:strongreject_score/_is_success` |
| generation outputs | EXIST | `FREE_GENERATION_RESULTS*.jsonl:generation_text` |
| training membership | EXIST (proxy) | seeded (42/43/44) vs `_UNSEEDED` (100/200/300) generation-seed files |
| **objective_type** | **DERIVED** | from `objective.lambda_repr/lambda_refusal_dir/repr_at_cot_pos` + manifest `cot_target` (see §rule below) |
| **universality** | **DERIVED** | # behaviors in optimization manifest (1 = per_behavior, >1 = universal). `selection_mode` is ~always `weighted` and does NOT separate the two. |
| **category / origin_category** | **DERIVED** | `categorize()` LLM-read-through taxonomy — an analysis tool, NOT an official AdvBench field (none exists). |
| **lexical features** | **DERIVED** | pure-python featurizer over `suffix_str`/`suffix_ids` (§17.3F). |

Genuinely MISSING §17.1 columns (no on-disk source): secondary category, labeling confidence, labeling rationale (§17.2 asks for these; the taxonomy is single-label rule-based). No per-suffix human validation field exists.

**objective_type rule:** `lambda_repr>0 & lambda_refusal_dir>0 -> composite_repr+refusal_dir`; `lambda_refusal_dir>0 -> refusal_dir`; `lambda_repr>0 -> repr_match[_cot if repr_at_cot_pos]`; else pure target CE -> `cot_prefix_ce` if the manifest target is a `<think>` CoT prefix, else `prefix_ce`.

## §17.3B Cross-category transfer matrix

Full matrix in `results/CATEGORY_TRANSFER_MATRIX.csv`. `multi_instruction` origin = universal 5A suffix on full-520 (`outputs/stage_gcg_full/gcg_full_qwen3_7a_5a_full520/FREE_GENERATION_RESULTS.jsonl`, 1560 eval rows). Per-behavior origin rows come from the percot_v2 stratified sample (12 behaviors, best-candidate ASR from `outputs/stage_gcg_percot_v2/PERBEHAVIOR_ASR_RESULTS.jsonl`).

**Structural caveat:** on disk, each per-behavior suffix was evaluated ONLY on its own behavior, so per-behavior origin rows populate the **diagonal only** (i==j). True off-diagonal per-behavior transfer requires re-evaluating each suffix on other behaviors — not on disk (deferred). The `multi_instruction` row is the only fully populated cross-category row.

## §17.3C Single- vs multi-instruction suffixes

| metric | single (per-behavior) | multi (universal) |
|---|---|---|
| n suffixes | 249 | 87 |
| mean ASR | 0.3 (best-cand, n=12 beh, percot) | 0.0801 (full-520, n=1560 rows) |
| mean suffix_length | 20.0 | 19.6207 |
| mean non_ascii_frac | 0.0782 | 0.0932 |
| mean repeated_token_frac | 0.0598 | 0.0339 |
| frac has_prefill_phrase | 0.1446 | 0.1609 |
| frac has_imperative | 0.2048 | 0.2759 |

- Single-minus-multi ASR gap = **0.2199** (single = best-of-candidates per behavior on its OWN behavior, an upper bound; multi = one fixed suffix averaged over 520 held-in behaviors — the two ASRs are NOT strictly comparable; see caveat).
- Caveat: the single-instruction number is a per-behavior best-candidate ASR on the training behavior itself (optimistic); the multi number is a genuine many-behavior average. Use for direction, not as a like-for-like effect size.
- **Model-family caveat:** the `single` group is 100% qwen3 (249/249) while the `multi`/universal group pools 67 qwen3 + 18 gemma4 + 2 deepseek_r1, so any single-vs-multi contrast — including the §17.3F lexical means below — partly confounds universality with model family. The direction of the lexical gaps is robust (restricting `multi` to qwen3 does not reverse them), but treat their magnitudes as family-confounded.

## §17.3D Train vs unseen (generation-seed hold-out)

`training membership` here = generation seed set: seeded 42/43/44 (development) vs `_UNSEEDED` 100/200/300 (held-out), same fixed universal suffix on the same behaviors.

| set | file | optimized_asr | neutral_asr | n behaviors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| seeded_train_42_43_44 | `outputs/stage_gcg_full/gcg_full_qwen3_7a_5a_full520/FREE_GENERATION_RESULTS.jsonl` | 0.0801 | 0.0218 | 520 |
| unseen_100_200_300 | `outputs/stage_gcg_full/gcg_full_qwen3_7a_5a_full520/FREE_GENERATION_RESULTS_UNSEEDED.jsonl` | 0.0892 | 0.0383 | 493 |

Note: this measures generation-seed robustness of an already-fixed suffix, NOT transfer to unseen *instructions*. Genuine unseen-instruction transfer for the universal suffix is the multi_instruction row of §17.3B (evaluated on all 520, most of which were not in the 25-behavior optimization manifest `advbench_cot_target_manifest.jsonl`).

**Caveat (§17.3F, mandatory):** these are surface-form correlations only. Lexical commonality (e.g. a 'Sure'/prefill phrase or high non-ASCII fraction) does NOT imply any causal mechanism; mechanistic attribution requires the internal-state analysis deferred below.

## §17.3E & §17.4 — Deferred to mechanistic hand-off

§17.3E (universality-rank vs attention/internal-state/refusal-direction effects) and the §17.4 mechanistic representative-subset analysis require GPU activations and are OUT OF SCOPE for this CPU-only phase. `results/SUFFIX_TAXONOMY.csv` (with universality + objective_type + refusal-dir config columns) is the selection table for that hand-off.
